title: Handbag that's a rucksack type for a laptop

posts.author: Willitevergrowback
posts.paraphrase: Opening post. They travel to London for work once or twice a month and want one rucksack-style bag that works as both handbag and laptop bag, so they can be hands-free on the Tube and not carry a separate handbag and laptop bag.
posts.quote: don’t want to take a separate handbag and laptop bag

posts.author: Usernamenotfound1
posts.paraphrase: They doubt one bag can be both. They use a North Face rucksack for the laptop and put a handbag inside the rucksack when travelling.
posts.quote: but a rucksack which will carry a laptop is not a handbag.

posts.author: BlackSwan
posts.paraphrase: They own a plain July backpack with a laptop sleeve and recommend the more stylish July Juliette Soft Backpack.
posts.quote: but this one is more stylish.

posts.author: Xiaoxiong
posts.paraphrase: They mention the Knomo Beauchamp, popular a couple of years ago for its handbag-like look, but say it is clearly a rucksack. They are considering a convertible backpack-to-shoulder-bag from Italian Handbag Company.
posts.quote: very definitely a rucksack rather than a handbag though.

posts.author: SheilaFentiman
posts.paraphrase: They suggest a Bellroy Lite Totepack, which can be carried as a rucksack or a tote.
posts.quote: Something like this that can be carried as a rucksack or a tote?

posts.author: BoswellTheScribe
posts.paraphrase: They recommend Roka's work backpacks.
posts.quote: Roka make great bags.

posts.author: nonanny
posts.paraphrase: They bought a Fat Face Ava black leather backpack for their London trips; it fits a 14-inch laptop, looks like a handbag and is soft leather.
posts.quote: is like a handbag.

posts.author: LittlePinkDinosaur
posts.paraphrase: They are a teacher and use a Lekesky 15.6-inch rucksack for laptop, diary and school items; it is not really a handbag but looks nicer than a standard practical rucksack.
posts.quote: Slightly nicer than a standard 'practical' rucksack.

posts.author: Lola888
posts.paraphrase: They saw many bags like this in Hong Kong but cannot find good ones online, and advise searching for a 2-in-1 or convertible bag.
posts.quote: You want a 2 in 1 or convertible bag.

posts.author: countrybump
posts.paraphrase: They switched away from a tote because carrying it over one arm gave them recurring pain and numbness in their hand. They bought an Oliver Bonas Ethel black backpack in the station after checking it fitted a laptop, and still use it.
posts.quote: getting pain and numbness in my hand on and off

posts.author: previouslyknownas
posts.paraphrase: They use a Mia Tui Dolly quilted laptop tote (large and small) and several other Mia Tui bags, and praise their practicality, looks and customer service.
posts.quote: and there customer service is fab

posts.author: Orangeandpinkcloud
posts.paraphrase: They recommend the White Stuff Sophia leather backpack in mid tan; they own it in blue.
posts.quote: white stuff here! Although mine is blue.

posts.author: QueenOfThorns
posts.paraphrase: They own the Oliver Bonas Mami black laptop backpack, which comes in several colours.
posts.quote: It comes in four or five different colours

posts.author: Manythingsgoingon
posts.paraphrase: They own two Radley backpacks in the smart leather versions for work; both easily fit a laptop and work as a handbag or backpack.
posts.quote: They easily fit my laptop

posts.author: Oceangrey
posts.paraphrase: They recommend the Artisan Stories Cleo convertible leather backpack-tote; its straps cross over, which they say stops people stealing from it on the Tube.
posts.quote: the straps cross over so no one can steal from you on the tube.

posts.author: Willitevergrowback
posts.paraphrase: Thread starter says the suggestions are exactly the kind of bag they were looking for and asks for more.
posts.quote: exactly the type of thing I was looking for

posts.author: shrodingersvaccine
posts.paraphrase: They suggest a Fossil Parker or an Elina bag. Their Elina converts to a tote and has survived 2.5 years of daily use, including coffee spills and overstuffing, and still looks new.
posts.quote: still looks brand new!

posts.author: DramaAlpaca
posts.paraphrase: They use a Roka Blackfriars messenger bag in an older ash recycled-canvas colourway, which holds everything they need.
posts.quote: it holds everything

posts.author: TeenLifeMum
posts.paraphrase: They have a green bag that is two years old and still looks new; they like the soft leather and the pocket layout.
posts.quote: 2 years on it still looks new

posts.author: Verv
posts.paraphrase: They recommend The Brown Buffalo Conceal Tote, a tote with a backpack harness that can be hidden away.
posts.quote: its an incredible bag.

posts.author: Healthyalltheway
posts.paraphrase: They recommend the Vestirsi Bella 3-in-1 convertible bag (backpack, crossbody, tote), sold in three sizes and many colours; they own an XL for conferences and a large for daily use.
posts.quote: these are amazing

posts.author: selffellatingouroborosofhate
posts.paraphrase: They suggest a Gregory Maya 20L hiking pack, not sold as a laptop bag; their laptop fits in the hydration-bladder pocket and the hip belt holds their wallet and phone.
posts.quote: It's not sold as a laptop bag

posts.author: Janefx40
posts.paraphrase: They own a bag mentioned earlier in the thread in red and love it; they nearly bought it in bottle green.
posts.quote: There was also a bottle green that I nearly got!

posts.author: HeNeedsRehab
posts.paraphrase: They ask owners of the Oliver Bonas Mami what laptop size fits, because the listing does not say and their new laptop is very large.
posts.quote: Annoyingly the description doesn’t say and my new laptop is bloody massive

posts.author: COUNCAT14
posts.paraphrase: They recommend the Poppy and Peonies Commuter Backpack in black, which they have used for the same purpose for two years; they like its many pockets and colour range and expect several more years of use.
posts.quote: I have this for exactly the same purpose and can’t recommend it enough!

posts.author: HeNeedsRehab
posts.paraphrase: They respond enthusiastically to the Poppy and Peonies suggestion.
posts.quote: Ooh yes this is great!

posts.author: SpecialBreak
posts.paraphrase: They suggest Stackers, which come in many sizes and styles, and link a Stackers luxury backpack.
posts.quote: Stackers! Many different sizes and styles….

posts.author: Triskellion75
posts.paraphrase: They own a Stackers bag and like it, but their fairly large laptop takes up a lot of the space inside.
posts.quote: My laptop is fairly big which takes up a good amount of room though.

posts.author: QueenOfThorns
posts.paraphrase: Answering about the Oliver Bonas Mami, they say their 15-inch laptop fits; a slightly larger laptop would probably fit too, but not much more.
posts.quote: Mine is 15 inch, so not massive.

posts.author: weirdoboelady
posts.paraphrase: They own the Dr. Martens Kiev smooth leather laptop backpack in chestnut brown; it is plainly a rucksack but very attractive, strangers often compliment it, and it is very comfortable.
posts.quote: it's so beautiful that I've lost count of the number of times total strangers have admired it

posts.author: Runningshoes99
posts.paraphrase: They own the Sandqvist 14-inch leather-lid backpack in black; its inner laptop sleeve means no separate case is needed, and it is lighter than all-leather bags, which suits the amount of walking they do.
posts.quote: has an inner laptop sleeve which means you don’t need a case

posts.author: HeNeedsRehab
posts.paraphrase: They report that reviews of the Poppy and Peonies backpack are very poor.
posts.quote: Reviews on the Poppy and Peonies one are shockingly bad

posts.author: selffellatingouroborosofhate
posts.paraphrase: They realise their idea of a handbag is very different from other posters' ideas.
posts.quote: Reading this thread, it's dawning on me that my idea of "handbag" is nothing like anyone else's.

posts.author: MojoMoon
posts.paraphrase: They suggest more expensive options: the Alemi Zurich Viadukt Day in cognac leather and the Eeva-Ria CI2 in black croc-effect.
posts.quote: Spendier options:

posts.author: PretzelChoc
posts.paraphrase: They prefer shoulder bags to backpacks, ideally ones that slot onto a wheelie case, with strong sewn-in or sling-style straps, and carry a separate cross-body bag for valuables; they are not asked to remove the bag on planes. They recommend a cheaper Jooeer waterproof laptop tote and advise trying cheaper designs first, as they had to try several types before finding what they liked.
posts.quote: I found I had to try a few different types of bag before I found what I liked

posts.author: Loiste
posts.paraphrase: They have just bought the Misako Dominica backpack, which has a 14-inch laptop pocket and can be carried as a shoulder bag; it fits their 13-inch laptop plus a bit more, is lightweight and good for journeys.
posts.quote: Fits my brief - fits 13 inch laptop and a bit more, good for journeys and lightweight.

posts.author: Sofuckingsad
posts.paraphrase: They own a bag mentioned in the thread and carry their laptop in it all the time, and recommend it, but warn to measure the laptop first because the bag's opening is fairly small and there is no padding or laptop protection.
posts.quote: you need to measure carefully as the ‘mouth’ of the bag isn’t huge

posts.author: barofsoap
posts.paraphrase: They recommend Roka.
posts.quote: definitely ROKA

posts.author: drspouse
posts.paraphrase: They own an older Radley backpack that fits a laptop but has no padded compartment; they cannot provide a link.
posts.quote: I have a Radley backpack that fits a laptop.
